mainTopic: Knowing to transfer ownership of a document, and divorcing a wife by giving her a slave or courtyard holding the גט.
overview: The גמרא is looking for proof that people know they must transfer ownership of a document, such as a גט. The proof from an old man is rejected because an old man is different. רבא then brings a proof from an ערב, but רב אשי rejects it because a man is different. רב אשי instead brings a proof from a משנה that says a woman may write her own גט. Next, רבא rules that if a husband puts a גט in his slave's hand, or in his courtyard, and gives it to his wife with a gift document, she is divorced. The גמרא explains that the slave case only works when the slave is tied up (כפות), and it shows why רבא needed to teach both cases. אביי objects that a חצר is learned from 'her hand,' which works even against her will, while a gift needs her consent. רב שימי בר אשי challenges אביי from a שליח לקבלה, and the גמרא gives two answers in defense of אביי. The amud ends as the גמרא starts a question on the משנה's list of things a גט may be written on, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: An old man is different
steps.stepSummary: The proof from the case of an old man is pushed off, because an old man knows to transfer ownership.
steps.simpleTranslation: An old man is different, because he knows to transfer ownership.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof it just brought from the case of an old man (זקן). An experienced old man knows to transfer ownership of the document, so his case proves nothing about ordinary people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether we can assume people know to transfer ownership of a document, like a גט. The old man's case does not prove this, because he may be unusually knowledgeable. We still need a case that shows ordinary people do this.

keyTerms.meaning: An old man; here, an experienced person who knows the law
Is different
To transfer ownership

phrases.english: An old man is different,
since he knows to transfer ownership.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the earlier proof from the old man, which came before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the old man's case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An expert old man may know to transfer ownership, while ordinary people may not.

steps.title: רבא's proof from a guarantor who signs later
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a new proof from the case of an ערב who joined after the document was signed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: There is a proof from here. A guarantor who appears after the documents were signed collects only from free, unsold property.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries a new proof. He uses the rule about an ערב who joins after the loan document was already signed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Such an ערב's obligation can only be collected from נכסים בני חורין, his property that was never sold. רבא reads this case as showing that ordinary people know to transfer ownership of the document so that the guarantee takes effect. So, he says, ordinary people do know to transfer ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantor on a loan
The signing of the documents
Free property, meaning property that was not sold to others
From here; introduces a proof

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: From here —
a guarantor who appears after the signing of the documents,
phrases.notes: Literally "who comes out": the guarantor's name shows up on the document only after the witnesses already signed.

phrases.english: collects from free property!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof from the old man with a new proof.
steps.raayaObject: That ordinary people know to transfer ownership of a document.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that an ערב who joins after the signing collects from נכסים בני חורין.

steps.title: רב אשי: a man is different
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects רבא's proof: a man may know to transfer ownership, but that does not prove a woman does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: What is the difficulty? Maybe a man is different, because he knows to transfer ownership!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes off רבא's proof. The ערב case involves men, and a man may know to transfer ownership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our question is about a woman and her גט. A man dealing with loans may know these money rules better, so his case does not prove what a woman would know. This is the same kind of rejection as the old man in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difficulty? Here it means: this is no proof
Perhaps
A man

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: What is the difficulty?
phrases.notes: He means: why is this case a proof at all?

phrases.english: Perhaps a man is different, since he knows to transfer ownership!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof using the same reasoning used against the old man.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case involves a man, who may know the law. It tells us nothing about a woman.

steps.title: רב אשי's proof: a woman may write her own גט
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי proves from a משנה that a woman may write her own גט, which shows that she knows to transfer it to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: There is a proof from here. A woman may write her own גט, and a man may write his own receipt, because a גט is made valid only by the witnesses who sign it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a better proof, from a case about a woman herself. A woman may write her own גט, and a man may write his own receipt (שובר).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Who writes the document does not matter, because a גט becomes valid only through its signing witnesses. If a woman writes her own גט, she must then transfer it to her husband so he can give it to her. So the משנה assumes that a woman, too, knows to transfer ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: A receipt; here, the wife's receipt that she was paid her כתובה
What makes the גט valid
Its signers, meaning the witnesses

steps.whatToRemember: The old man proof and רבא's guarantor proof both failed, because those people may simply know the law. רב אשי's proof works because it comes from a case about a woman herself.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said: From here —
a woman may write her own bill of divorce,
and the man may write his receipt,
since a bill of divorce is made valid only by its signers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof with one that involves a woman directly.
steps.raayaObject: That a woman knows to transfer ownership of the גט to her husband.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: a woman may write her own גט, since a גט is valid only through its signing witnesses.

steps.title: A גט placed in a slave's hand, then the slave given to the wife
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if a husband puts a גט in his slave's hand and gives the slave to his wife with a gift document, she acquires the slave and is divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If he wrote her a גט, put it in his slave's hand, and wrote her a gift document giving her the slave, she acquires the slave and is divorced by the גט.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבא gives a ruling about a גט that reaches the wife through a slave who becomes hers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the wife owns the slave through the שטר מתנה, the slave counts as her property. The גט in his hand is therefore treated as being in her domain, like a גט placed in her courtyard. So she is divorced right away.

keyTerms.meaning: His slave
A gift document
She acquired him
She is divorced

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a woman can receive her גט through something she owns, not only by having it handed to her.

phrases.english: Rava said: If he wrote her a bill of divorce,
and placed it in the hand of his slave,
and wrote her a deed of gift for him,
phrases.notes: "For him" means the slave: the gift document gives her the slave.

phrases.english: she acquired him, and she is divorced by it.
phrases.notes: "By it" means the גט that is in the slave's hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כָּתַב לָהּ גֵּט, וּנְתָנוֹ בְּיַד עַבְדּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion about transferring ownership ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a husband gives his wife the slave holding her גט by means of a gift document, she acquires the slave and is divorced immediately.

steps.title: A slave is a moving courtyard, so how can he acquire the גט?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's ruling: a slave is like a moving courtyard, and a moving courtyard cannot acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why should she acquire the גט? The slave is a moving courtyard, and a moving courtyard does not acquire!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's ruling from Step 5. It asks how the slave can acquire the גט for the wife if a slave counts as a 'moving courtyard'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person's courtyard can acquire things for him, and a slave is treated like property in the same way. But a courtyard only works when it stays in one place. A slave walks around, so he should be a חצר מהלכת, which cannot acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: And why? Opens a challenge
Courtyard. A person's property that can acquire items placed in it for him
A moving courtyard, which cannot acquire

phrases.english: And why?
phrases.notes: He means: why should the wife get the גט through the slave in רבא's case?

phrases.english: It is a moving courtyard,
and a moving courtyard does not acquire!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling about the slave
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the wife acquires the slave and is divorced by the גט in his hand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A slave acquires like a courtyard, but he moves around, and a moving courtyard cannot acquire

steps.title: Even a standing slave counts as a moving courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks the possible answer that the slave was standing still, using another rule of רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say it was a slave who was standing, didn't רבא say: anything that would not acquire when walking also does not acquire when standing or sitting!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an answer, that the slave was standing still, and then rejects it right away. This makes the question from Step 6 even stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא himself taught that if something cannot acquire while moving, it also cannot acquire while standing or sitting. What matters is that the slave is able to move, not whether he is moving right now. So a standing slave does not solve the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say. Brings up a possible answer, usually to reject it
Standing
Sitting
Walking, moving

phrases.english: And if you will say: in a standing one,
phrases.notes: He means a slave who was standing still when he got the גט.

phrases.english: but didn't Rava say:
anything that would not acquire if it were walking,
does not acquire when standing or sitting!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects a possible defense against the challenge in Step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested answer that רבא spoke about a standing slave
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא's own rule says that anything unable to acquire while moving also cannot acquire while standing or sitting

steps.title: רבא's ruling is about a tied-up slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבא was speaking about a slave who was tied up and could not move.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the law is in the case of a bound slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: רבא's ruling is about a slave who is tied up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tied-up slave cannot move at all, so he is not a moving courtyard. He works like a regular courtyard that stays in one place, and he can acquire the גט for the wife.

keyTerms.meaning: The law. Here it means the ruling that רבא taught
Bound, tied up and unable to move

phrases.english: And the law is in a bound one.
phrases.notes: He means רבא's ruling was said about a slave who is tied up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 6 and 7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's slave was an ordinary slave who could move, so he should not acquire
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא spoke about a tied-up slave, who cannot move and acquires like a fixed courtyard
steps.whatToRemember: The slave in רבא's case only works because he is כפות. A slave who can move, even one standing still, counts as a חצר מהלכת and cannot acquire.

steps.title: רבא: giving her a courtyard with the גט inside
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if the husband puts a גט in his courtyard and gives her the courtyard with a gift document, she acquires it and is divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: If he wrote her a גט and placed it in his courtyard, and wrote her a gift document for the courtyard, she acquires it and is divorced by it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling that matches his slave ruling, but with a courtyard instead of a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband does not hand her the גט directly. He gives her a courtyard that has the גט inside it. When she acquires the courtyard through the שטר מתנה, the courtyard acquires the גט for her, so she is divorced.

keyTerms.meaning: His courtyard
Gift document, a written deed that gives property
She acquired it
She is divorced

phrases.english: And Rava said:
If he wrote her a bill of divorce
and put it in his courtyard,
and wrote her a gift document on it,
phrases.notes: 'On it' means on the courtyard. He is giving her the courtyard as a gift.

phrases.english: she has acquired it,
and is divorced by it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: כָּתַב לָהּ גֵּט וּנְתָנוֹ בַּחֲצֵרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling of רבא, using a courtyard in place of a slave
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband can divorce his wife by giving her, through a gift document, a courtyard that contains the גט

steps.title: Why רבא had to teach both the slave and the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that each ruling was needed, because without it we might have thought the חכמים made a גזירה against that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both are necessary. If he had taught us only a slave, I would have said only a slave works, but for a courtyard we should make a decree because of her courtyard that comes later. And if he had taught us only a courtyard, I would have said only a courtyard works, but for a slave we should decree against a bound one because of one that is not bound. So he teaches us both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: why did רבא need two rulings that seem to say the same thing? It shows that each case has its own reason for a possible גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a courtyard, people might mix this up with a case where the גט was lying somewhere and the yard only became hers later. With a slave, people might mix up a tied-up slave with a free-moving one, who cannot acquire. רבא's two rulings teach that the חכמים made neither גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary. Explains why two similar teachings are both needed
I would have said. Introduces a mistaken first thought
Let us make a decree, a rabbinic safeguard
Because of, so people won't confuse it with
He teaches us, which rules out the mistaken thought

phrases.english: And it is necessary;
for if he had taught us only a slave,
I would have said: specifically a slave,
but a courtyard: let us make a decree,
because of her courtyard that comes afterward;
phrases.notes: This means a yard where the גט was already lying, which only became hers later. That would not count as her husband giving it to her.

phrases.english: and if he had taught us only a courtyard,
I would have said: specifically a courtyard,
but a slave: let us decree against a bound one
because of one that is not bound;
so he teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the slave ruling and the courtyard ruling were both needed
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא, showing why each teaching is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each case alone might have been forbidden by a גזירה: the courtyard because of a yard acquired later, the slave because of an untied slave
steps.terutzMaskana: No גזירה was made. Both the courtyard and the tied-up slave are valid ways to divorce
steps.whatToRemember: רבא taught both cases because each has its own possible גזירה. The courtyard could be confused with a yard that became hers later, and the tied-up slave with one who is not tied. The חכמים made neither גזירה.

steps.title: A courtyard must work like her hand, but a gift needs her consent
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that a חצר given as a gift cannot receive a גט. A חצר is learned from 'her hand,' which works even against her will, while a gift only works with her consent.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Where do we learn that a courtyard can receive a גט? From the word 'her hand.' So just as her hand takes things for her whether she agrees or not, her courtyard must also take things for her whether she agrees or not. But a gift only works if she agrees. It does not work against her will!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's ruling from Step 9 about giving her the courtyard as a gift. He says a gift-courtyard does not fit the source that teaches חצר works at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason a חצר can receive a גט is that it counts as an extension of her hand (ידה). Her hand receives a גט even against her will. A gift, though, only becomes hers if she agrees. So a courtyard she owns only through a gift is not like her hand, and it should not be able to receive the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: Courtyard; property that can acquire things for its owner
Was included (learned from a word in the פסוק)
With her consent
Against her will
A gift

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying a woman can't be divorced through her courtyard. He agrees a חצר works. He is only objecting to a courtyard she got as a gift, because owning it depended on her agreeing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a key rule for the rest of the sugya: anything learned from 'her hand' must work the way her hand works, both with her consent and against her will.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Now, from where was a courtyard included? From 'her hand';
phrases.notes: From the פסוק about giving a גט 'in her hand' (דברים 24:1).

phrases.english: just as her hand, which works
whether with her consent or against her will,
so too her courtyard must be something that works
whether with her consent or against her will;
but a gift works only with her consent,
and against her will it does not work!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מִכְּדֵי חָצֵר מֵהֵיכָא אִיתְרַבַּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's gift-courtyard ruling from Step 9 based on the source for חצר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a courtyard given as a gift can receive a גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חצר comes from 'her hand,' which works even against her will. A gift needs her consent, so a gift-courtyard does not match its source.

steps.title: But an agent for receiving also needs her consent
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי objects to אביי. A שליח לקבלה only works if she appoints him, yet he can still receive her גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי objected: But look at an agent for receiving the גט. He only works with her consent, not against her will, and still he is a valid agent to receive it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי attacks אביי's reasoning. He shows a way of receiving a גט that needs her consent and still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said anything that receives a גט must work even against her will, like her hand. But a שליח לקבלה only exists if she chooses to appoint him, and he is still valid. So, רב שימי argues, the comparison to her hand cannot be total.

keyTerms.meaning: Objected to it (a challenge to the previous reasoning)
Agency for receiving a גט on the woman's behalf
Agent

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi objected to it:
But what about agency for receipt,
which works with her consent but not against her will,
and yet he is a valid agent for receipt!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's rule from Step 11 with a counterexample.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that every way of receiving a גט must work even against her will.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שליח לקבלה needs her consent and still works, so needing consent does not disqualify a method.

steps.title: Agency comes from a different word in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that שליחות is not learned from 'her hand.' It is learned from the word ושלחה, so it does not have to follow the rules of her hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי would answer: Is agency learned from 'her hand'? No! It is learned from 'and he sends her' (ושלחה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives אביי's defense against רב שימי's challenge. The two cases come from different sources in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only methods learned from 'her hand' must match her hand and work even against her will. שליחות comes from a separate word, ושלחה, so it has its own rules and can require her consent. A חצר, though, does come from 'her hand,' so אביי's objection to the gift-courtyard still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (introduces a rejected assumption)
'And he sends her,' the word in the פסוק that teaches agency

steps.whatToRemember: A חצר is learned from 'her hand,' so it must work even against her will. שליחות is learned from ושלחה, so it can depend on her consent. That is why אביי still holds that a gift-courtyard cannot receive a גט.

phrases.english: And Abaye? Is that to say agency is included from 'her hand'?!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is giving the answer אביי would say back to רב שימי.

phrases.english: It is included from 'and he sent,' 'and he sends her'!
phrases.notes: The פסוק (דברים 24:1) says וְשִׁלְּחָהּ, not just וְשִׁלַּח. The extra wording teaches that a שליח can be used.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שימי בר אשי's challenge in Step 12 and defends אביי's challenge from Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different sources: agency is learned from a separate word in the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every way of receiving a גט comes from 'her hand' and must follow its rules, so agency would disprove אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Agency comes from ושלחה and may need her consent. A חצר comes from 'her hand' and must work even against her will.

steps.title: A father can receive a גט for his young daughter against her will
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: שליחות לקבלה can also work against her will, because a father receives a גט for his minor daughter whether she wants it or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say this: we do find that receiving a גט through an agent can happen against her will. A father receives a גט for his young daughter even when she does not want it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to answer רב שימי בר אשי's objection. It shows that receiving a גט for a woman can work even against her will.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13, אביי said שליחות comes from a different פסוק, so it does not need to work like 'her hand.' This answer takes a different path. It says שליחות לקבלה really does work like 'her hand,' because a father can receive for his minor daughter without her consent. Either way, אביי's main point still stands: a חצר given as a gift needs her agreement, so it cannot receive a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say.' This opens a second, separate answer.
Against her will, without her agreement
Agency for receiving a גט on the woman's behalf
A father receives a גט on behalf of his daughter
A minor girl, under the age of maturity

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for אביי. First, שליחות comes from ושלחה, so it has its own rules. Second, שליחות can also work against her will, as with a father and his young daughter. Both answers leave אביי's point in place: a gifted חצר, which needs her consent, cannot receive a גט.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer is not against אביי. It defends him in a different way from step 13. It shows there is no real exception to the rule that receiving a גט can happen against her will.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
agency for receiving, too,
we have found works against her will,
phrases.notes: So receiving through an agent fits the 'her hand' pattern after all. Her hand works even when she doesn't agree.

phrases.english: since a father receives a bill of divorce
for his minor daughter against her will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer, different from step 13, to רב שימי בר אשי's objection in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-example: it shows that the supposed exception (agency that needs her consent) actually also exists against her will.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שליחות לקבלה seems to work only when she appoints the agent, so it would not match the 'her hand' rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Receiving a גט through someone else can work against her will, as with a father for his minor daughter. So it fits 'her hand,' and אביי's objection to the gifted חצר stands.

steps.title: Starting to question the משנה's case of a slave's hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about writing a גט on an olive leaf and begins a question with 'Granted, the hand of a slave.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said a גט may be written on an olive leaf, and so on. Granted, the hand of a slave...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next part of the משנה, which lists objects a גט can be written on. It opens with 'Granted,' which sets up a question that continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בשלמא means 'I understand this case, but...' Here the גמרא says it understands the case of a slave's hand. It is getting ready to ask about a different case in the same משנה. The actual question comes right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive leaf. The משנה allows a גט to be written on it.
'Etc.' The rest of the משנה's words are understood.
'Granted.' It accepts one case and leads into a question on another.
The hand of a slave. One of the things the משנה says a גט can be written on.

phrases.english: On the olive leaf, etc.:
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which allows writing a גט on an olive leaf, a cow's horn, or a slave's hand.

phrases.english: Granted, the hand of a slave
